questions.stem: You are caring for a 65-year-old. He reports that he started having chest pain that sounds like classic angina. After 2 minutes, the angina subsides. This exertional limitation has been stable over the last year and he does not experience chest pain at other times. He is on no medications. You refer him for coronary angiography, which demonstrates a 70% stenosis in his mid-left anterior descending coronary artery. Left ventriculography shows normal ventricular systolic function. What is the next most reasonable course of action from those listed below?

options.label: A
options.text: Advise him to stop playing tennis

options.label: C
options.text: Initiate anti-anginal medical therapy with a beta blocker, statin, and aspirin

options.label: D
options.text: Percutaneous coronary intervention with a drug-eluting stent
